items.title: Iran seeking 'harder targets' for attacks abroad, UK warns
items.summary: The warning from the head of the UK's domestic security agency comes after PM Burnham said an attempted plot at an air force base hosting US bombers was "almost certainly" coordinated in Tehran The leader of the UK's MI5 domestic security service on Tuesday said that Iran is expanding the scope of the hybrid attacks that it coordinates in the UK and elsewhere In an annual address outlining his assessment of threats to the UK , MI5 chief Ken McCallum said a "major shift this year has been Iranian ambitions to come at harder targets, like military sites." The remarks come after the US removed about a dozen long-range bombers from Fairford air base in the southern UK last week following an incident on September 27 during which several men were arrested on "suspicion of terrorism offenses." items.title: Mozambique: IPEME and TFO Canada launch TRISEG to boost MSME growth
items.summary: Funded by the Government of Canada, the TRISEG initiative aims to strengthen micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and promote their access to international markets The event was attended by IPEME Deputy Director-General Mijóia Caetano, Canada’s Ambassador to Mozambique, Zaki Munshi, Pascale Thivierge, representing TFO Canada, and Brenda Garcia, the project manager at the same organisation The launch brought together various stakeholders to discuss the strengthening and development of MSMEs in Mozambique Running for five years (2025–2030), the TRISEG project aims to support 200 MSMEs in Mozambique, 67% of which will be owned or led by women and under-represented groups.

items.title: How will emergency rule in Pakistan's northwest affect Afghan ties?

items.title: DR Congo: Kabila’s move towards M23 raises questions over peace
items.summary: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political-military front that brings together the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 coalition. Analysts say it could reshape opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi Joseph Kabila's decision to lead a new political-military movement, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), puts the former president of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in more direct confrontation with President Felix Tshisekedi's government . Kabila announced the FRN on October 12 in Goma, eastern DRC, at his residence, where leaders of the AFC/M23 rebel movements joined him FRN coalition adviser, Claude Ibalanky, said the group would unite opposition forces, including figures associated with the AFC/M23 movement. The new structure succeeds the Congo River Alliance (AFC), which had been allied with the M23 rebellion. Its leadership includes former AFC leader Corneille Nangaa and M23 political leader Bertrand Bisimwa.

items.title: Chapo calls for mechanisms aimed at distinguishing competent teachers
items.summary: Maputo, 13 Out (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has urged the Ministry of Education to develop mechanisms aimed at recognizing teachers who distinguish themselves by merit, dedication, competence and responsibility. Speaking on Monday in Maputo, during the ceremony marking the Mozambican Teachers’ Day – which is celebrated on October 12 to commemorate the creation of the National Organization of Teachers (ONP) – career management requires more responsive, transparent and sustainable responses to the country’s education system. “The government is committed to continue to invest in education, in line with the country’s possibilities. The appreciation of teachers must be accompanied by fulfillment of professional duties, including ethics, integrity, assiduity and excellence quality of the teaching process”, he said. The day was celebrated at a moment when the country’s National Association of Teachers (ANAPRO) has been calling for a response to the long-running dispute over the government’s failure to pay teachers for overtime.

items.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
items.summary: File photo of gold prospectors in northern Sudan At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining site in Red Sea state on Saturday Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region "The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday.
